title: ARGENT & FAITH modern silver rosary capsule: neutralize an 8-piece two-session bench batch to an in-frame grey card, hold each finish true, then author the hero + vectorize the wordmark + data-merge one spec sheet per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com jewelry lead (a seller wanting a 'modern design for a rosary necklace,' silver as the primary material, a clean modern aesthetic, and 'good communication skills for revisions'). The raw brief literally asks to DESIGN/3D-model a piece of jewelry from scratch, which the connector surface grades out of scope (no text-to-image, no 3D, no from-scratch art), so the job is honestly re-cast to the in-scope production-art package a silver-jewelry seller commissions AROUND supplied studio captures — and SCALED UP from a single hero to the seller's whole modern-rosary CAPSULE so cross-asset colour consistency (the hardest, most gradeable thing) is actually present. The brand is laundered to a FICTIONAL house, ARGENT & FAITH (an invented descriptive name — 'argent' is generic French for silver — not a real company or trademark; web search returns no confusable jeweler). ENRICHMENT needed to make the chain concrete, failable, and measurable: the seller photographed EIGHT SKUs of one modern rosary family across TWO bench sessions under deliberately different mixed lighting (warm desk-lamp, cool window, green fluorescent, mixed/split), and clipped a neutral 18% grey card into the corner of every frame so white balance can be reconciled after the fact. The capsule ships in TWO real finishes — brushed/satin silver AND oxidized/antiqued (blackened) silver — which is the product truth the client sells and which the retouch must preserve. The client supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record spec-sheet template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (the per-SKU product photo and the shared masthead wordmark), the SKU roster as a CSV, the eight raw camera captures, and a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock. A necklace has ENCLOSED interior negative space (the loop centre, the gaps between links), which image_remove_background cannot punch see-through — so the hero is placed by image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) onto a solid neutral studio sweep where the enclosed interior correctly reads the sweep colour, and no see-through interior is ever claimed as a gate. Every transform below is a real, listed Adobe-connector capability: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no 3D, no from-scratch art, no compositing, no upscaling.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight ARGENT & FAITH rosary SKUs shot across two mismatched bench sessions to the 18% grey card each one carries so the capsule reads as one white point, decide per frame and per finish how to grade (brushed silver crisp and cool-neutral, oxidized silver held true and dark) with a masked metal look, place the flagship on a clean neutral studio sweep as a 4:5 e-commerce hero, cut a stamping line-art and a screen-print halftone, vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored InDesign template into one press-ready spec sheet per SKU.
full_brief:
ARGENT & FAITH is a small studio selling handcrafted modern silver religious jewelry — clean geometric links, minimal crucifixes — and we've just finalized a new modern-rosary capsule. We shot the whole line at our bench over two evenings and the folder is a mess: we grabbed whatever lamp was free, so some pieces came out warm and some cold, a couple are a touch bright and a couple flat, and one or two frames are crooked. Because we knew the light was inconsistent, we clipped a neutral 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. We are NOT reshooting, and we do NOT need any jewelry designed — the pieces exist; we need the commercial production art built around these captures for our store, our lookbook, a stamped/printed merch concept and our wholesale binder.

What we need back:

1. THE WHOLE CAPSULE, matched. Bring every one of the eight photos to a consistent, true-to-product studio look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the set will share one white point and one brightness so a customer scrolling the line can't tell which piece was shot on which night. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance and exposure decision to land on the shared target. Critically, our capsule ships in two real finishes — a bright brushed/satin silver AND an antiqued/oxidized (deliberately darkened) silver — and each piece must stay TRUE to its actual finish. Silver should read like silver, premium and clean; but do not 'brighten' a piece into a finish it isn't. When you're done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm they were matched, not eyeballed.

2. THE HERO. Take our flagship brushed piece and give us a retouched commercial hero: level, graded to the capsule look, the necklace lifted cleanly onto a distraction-free neutral studio sweep, reframed to the exact 4:5 e-commerce crop with breathing room, the grey card cropped out. The metal has to read crisp against the sweep, with the polished link highlights protected (not blown). Deliver the polished 4:5 JPEG plus the eight matched packshots for the listings and the sheets.

3. STAMPING + MERCH ART. From the hero, give us a clean vector line-art / silhouette of the necklace (SVG) we can scale for stamping and embroidery, and a single-tone screen-print / halftone tech graphic (PNG) for a tote/tee mockup and our stamping vendor.

4. THE WORDMARK. Our ARGENT & FAITH wordmark only exists as a flat desk scan on off-white paper, slightly skewed. Get it clean and razor-sharp as vector art for the sheet masthead and our woven labels — it must not look like a fuzzy scan when printed.

5. THE SPEC SHEETS. We've hand-built the InDesign spec-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the product photo, one for the wordmark at the top), and we're giving you the SKU roster. Merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its copy bound verbatim, its matching graded photo dropped in and the crisp wordmark in the masthead, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every SKU, one page per SKU, the flagship simply first. Bind our copy and prices verbatim — do not rewrite them.

Keep everything modern, minimal and silver-true. Strong communication for revisions is essential.

inputs.name: af201_brushed_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN sterling silver rosary necklace with clean geometric oval links, small smooth minimal beads and a flat minimalist modern crucifix, BRUSHED/satin silver finish (not high-polish), laid out on a dark slate bench. A standard 18% neutral grey card and a small white swatch sit flat in the lower-left corner of the frame as a reference. Shot under COOL north-window light with a distinct blue-cyan cast, slightly flat and marginally under-exposed, frame tilted about 4 degrees. Real metal micro-scratches, faint fingerprints, tiny dust, shallow imperfect focus, candid documentary product shot straight off the camera, NOT a clean ecommerce render, NOT CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-201, Session A (cool/blue), tilted ~4deg. THE FLAGSHIP — the hero, the line-art source and the halftone source all derive from this frame, and it is CSV row 1 so it becomes page 1 of the merged sheet. Brushed silver: the correct grade WARMS the temperature off the blue cast to the card, lifts exposure to the set brightness, then the masked metal look pulls residual warmth out of the metal and lifts it a touch so brushed silver reads crisp and cool-neutral. Its corrective is the OPPOSITE sign of the warm-lamp frames, so a single shared white balance across the batch cannot serve it. Real-camera scale so the 4:5 2400x3000 hero and the 300 DPI sheet frame are reachable by DOWNSCALE only. Grey card in frame is the neutralisation ground truth.

inputs.name: af202_brushed_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN brushed/satin silver rosary necklace (longer chain than AF-201, same geometric-link family, minimal modern crucifix) laid on the dark slate bench. A standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch sit in the corner of the frame. Shot under a WARM desk lamp with a strong amber cast, level, normal exposure. Real brushed-metal micro-texture, faint fingerprints and dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-202, Session B (warm/amber), level. Brushed silver under warm light: correct move is to COOL the temperature to neutralise the card (opposite direction to AF-201) then the masked metal look holds brushed silver bright-neutral. Proves the batch splits into opposite corrective directions.

inputs.name: af203_brushed_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN brushed/satin silver rosary necklace (longest chain in the family, geometric links, minimal crucifix) on the dark slate bench, a standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch in the frame corner. Shot under GREEN overhead fluorescent shop light with a distinct green/magenta-deficient cast, frame tilted about 3 degrees, normal exposure, slightly dull. Real metal micro-texture, dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-203, Session A (green fluorescent), tilted ~3deg. Its cast needs a TINT (green->magenta) correction, NOT a temperature move — a different colour axis from the warm/cool frames, forcing per-frame reasoning rather than one slider. Brushed silver held bright-neutral by the masked look.

inputs.name: af204_oxidized_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN OXIDIZED/antiqued (deliberately blackened, dark gunmetal patina) silver rosary necklace, same geometric-link modern family, minimal crucifix, laid on the dark slate bench. A standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch sit in the frame corner. Shot under WARM tungsten light with an orange cast, level, normal exposure. Real dark-patina metal with recessed blackening in the link crevices and brighter high points, faint dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-204, Session B (warm tungsten), level. THE FINISH TRAP. This piece is GENUINELY dark by design (oxidized/antiqued) — its darkness is the real product, not an exposure error, and its in-frame grey card is the honest neutral reference. The correct move: cool the warm cast until the card reads neutral, match set brightness, and HOLD the dark patina (the masked metal look must NOT lift/brighten it or chase a 'silver should be bright' idea). A naive agent that applies the same brighten-and-cool-to-crisp treatment used on the brushed SKUs will erase the patina and make an antiqued piece look like tarnished brushed silver — product misrepresentation, invisible until inspected against the finish. Decision is driven by THIS frame + finish, not the batch.

inputs.name: af205_oxidized_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN OXIDIZED/antiqued dark silver rosary necklace (shorter chain), geometric links, minimal crucifix, on the dark slate bench, a standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch in the frame corner. Shot under COOL north-window light with a blue cast, frame tilted about 3 degrees, normal exposure. Real blackened patina in the recesses with brighter raised edges, dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-205, Session A (cool/blue), tilted ~3deg. Oxidized finish AGAIN, but under the opposite (cool) cast to AF-204 — so it takes a warming correction to its card, unlike AF-204's cooling one, while STILL holding the dark patina. Reinforces both the per-frame WB divergence and the finish-hold decision; copying AF-204's numbers here fails on the WB axis.

inputs.name: af206_brushed_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN brushed/satin silver rosary necklace with an extra-minimal small crucifix, geometric links, on the dark slate bench, a standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch in the frame corner. Shot under WARM desk lamp, level, slightly OVER-exposed with a couple of bright specular glints on the polished bead edges. Real brushed texture, faint fingerprints, dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-206, Session B (warm), level, slightly over. Brushed silver: cool the warm cast to the card AND pull exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the bright specular glints and match set brightness — a tonal move on top of the WB move, different from the other brushed frames. Its polished edges are a highlight-protection check.

inputs.name: af207_polished_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN HIGH-POLISH (mirror-bright) silver rosary necklace, geometric links, minimal crucifix, on the dark slate bench, a standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch in the frame corner. Shot under COOL window light, frame tilted about 4 degrees, FLAT and slightly under-exposed so the mirror metal muddies. Real specular hotspots on the polished links at risk of clipping, dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-207, Session A (cool), tilted ~4deg, flat/under. High-polish (not brushed, not oxidized) — a third finish: warm to the card, lift exposure and add contrast to bring the mirror metal up WITHOUT clipping the specular hotspots (highlight discipline). Distinct decision again — the batch is three finishes under mixed light, so per-frame reasoning is unavoidable.

inputs.name: af208_oxidized_rosary_raw.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL DSLR studio capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a MODERN OXIDIZED/antiqued dark silver rosary necklace (mid-length chain), geometric links, minimal crucifix, on the dark slate bench, a standard 18% neutral grey card and white swatch in the frame corner. Shot under a MIX of cool window light on one side and warm lamp on the other so the cast is split and uneven, level, normal exposure. Real blackened patina, dust, candid documentary product shot, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU AF-208, Session mixed (split cool+warm), level. Oxidized finish under the hardest cast to neutralise — the two sides disagree, so the agent must balance temperature AND tint toward the card's neutral, accepting a compromise, while STILL holding the dark patina. Third oxidized piece: the finish-hold decision must generalise across three differently-lit antiqued frames.

inputs.name: argent_faith_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'ARGENT & FAITH' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: an elegant modern serif in deep charcoal ink, a small minimal cross glyph centred above the word. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is generous extra paper margin around the mark, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat solid-ink wordmark on off-white paper (slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/knock the off-white toward white, crop to the mark, remove_background to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type. Binds into every sheet's masthead via the @Wordmark image column (never free-form placement).

inputs.name: argent_spec_sheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait jewelry spec sheet — ONE SKU per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<sku>>, <<product_name>>, <<material>>, <<finish>>, <<chain_length>>, <<crucifix_size>>, <<wholesale_price>>, <<retail_price>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @image (that SKU's graded packshot) and a masthead image frame at the top bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Modern minimal charcoal/silver layout, brand wordmark area top-left. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge <<fields>> plus genuine @image-path columns; a convert_pdf_to_indd template with literal typed text would NOT bind (that path is banned as a merge target). TWO image columns (@image, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded packshot AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so both the chain-produced photo and the chain-produced wordmark reach the sheet as MERGE BINDS, the only connector-doable path since free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. Supplied as an input, not a chain output.

inputs.name: argent_sku_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns sku,product_name,material,finish,chain_length,crucifix_size,wholesale_price,retail_price,@image,@Wordmark holding 8 rows, one per SKU of the modern rosary family (AF-201..AF-208), row 1 the flagship brushed piece. Each row carries the product name, material ('Sterling silver 925'), the finish descriptor (the real finish of that piece), chain length (e.g. 45cm/50cm/55cm/60cm/65cm), crucifix size, a US-dollar wholesale price and retail price. The @image column names that SKU's graded packshot file (e.g. @af201_packshot.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's single-record sheet. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @argent_faith_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every sheet as a merge bind. Column header names must exactly match the template's <<fields>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Header names must exactly match the authored .indd field names and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct per-SKU photo, AND the shared wordmark. The 'finish' column is catalog copy bound verbatim (product data, not a retouch recipe). @image points at the produced packshots; @Wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all 8 rows. 8 rows => the merge must produce exactly 8 finished sheets (page-count = row-count).

outputs.name: rosary_hero_4x5.jpg
outputs.spec: Retouched commercial hero of the flagship brushed piece (AF-201), 4:5 (2400x3000) JPEG sRGB: straightened, neutralised to its in-frame grey card (silver-true, no residual cast), graded to the capsule look with the brushed metal read crisp and cool-neutral via the masked metal pass and the polished link highlights protected (not clipped), the necklace isolated onto a clean neutral studio sweep via image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) — the enclosed loop interior correctly reads the solid sweep colour (no see-through interior is claimed) — reframed to the exact 4:5 e-commerce crop with breathing room by downscale/crop of camera-scale pixels (gen-free, no invented pixels), grey card cropped OUT of frame.

outputs.name: packshots_matched_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralised rosary packshots (AF-201..AF-208), each isolated onto the ARGENT & FAITH neutral studio sweep and matched to ONE shared white point and brightness across the whole capsule, with each piece's TRUE finish preserved (brushed crisp and cool-neutral, high-polish clean, oxidized held genuinely dark) — delivered as the sweep-placed product crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge via @image, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralised masters (card still in frame) the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, TWO SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation and finish-truth are graded on the RETAINED card-bearing neutralised master of each frame — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance) with the whole set matched to one white point, and the oxidized SKUs remain measurably darker than the brushed/polished SKUs (finish not flattened); (b) card-exclusion is checked SEPARATELY on each delivered sweep-placed product crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance/exposure move applied per frame and the per-finish metal move.

outputs.name: rosary_lineart.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector line-art / silhouette SVG of the flagship necklace for stamping and embroidery, traced only after the hero cut-out is knocked to transparency and cropped to the mark's tight bounds (prep-before-trace). A single solid silhouette by design — the necklace's enclosed loop centre and inter-link gaps read as filled shape (image_remove_background cannot punch enclosed interior holes), which is the correct form for a stamping/embroidery silhouette; no see-through interior is claimed.

outputs.name: rosary_halftone_tech.png
outputs.spec: Single-tone screen-print / halftone tech graphic PNG of the flagship necklace (image_apply_halftone on the prepared hero cut-out) for a tote/tee merch mockup and the stamping vendor.

outputs.name: argent_faith_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the ARGENT & FAITH wordmark, traced only after the flat scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Binds into every sheet's masthead via @Wordmark and serves the woven-label deliverable.

outputs.name: argent_spec_sheets_perSKU.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly EIGHT press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait spec sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8, the flagship AF-201 simply page 1) — exported by document_render_layout from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its sku/product_name/material/finish/chain_length/crucifix_size/wholesale_price/retail_price verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralised packshot dropped into the product image frame (via @image) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the masthead frame (via @Wordmark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality at the frame trim.

Prep-before-trace: crop the transparent cut-out to the necklace's tight bounds so vectorize and halftone act only on the mark, not empty canvas. Feeds both the line-art and the halftone.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and cross glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining. One batch upload (1) fans into eight per-SKU grade sub-chains: image_auto_straighten on the tilted frames only (2-5: AF-201/203/205/207), then image_apply_adjustments neutralises each frame to its own in-frame grey card (6-13, each consuming the straightened frame where one exists else the uploaded raw), then image_select_by_prompt builds a metal mask per frame (14-21), then masked image_adjust_hsl drives the metal to the studio-silver target while holding each piece's TRUE finish (22-29) — the eight matched, finish-true masters. Each _house master is knocked onto the neutral studio sweep with image_remove_background({backgroundColor}) (30-37), then cropped to the shared packshot frame with the card removed (38-45 => packshots_matched_x8 and the eight @image cells). The flagship AF-201 additionally fans out: its swept master is reframed to the 4:5 e-commerce hero (46 => rosary_hero_4x5.jpg), and its _house master runs a prep-before-trace derivative chain — remove_background to transparency (47) -> crop_to_bounds (48) -> vectorize (49 => rosary_lineart.svg) and apply_halftone (50 => rosary_halftone_tech.png). The wordmark runs its own prep-before-trace chain from the uploaded scan: auto_straighten (51) -> apply_adjustments crisp (52) -> crop_to_bounds (53) -> remove_background to transparency (54) -> vectorize (55 => argent_faith_wordmark.svg). The eight packshots and the wordmark SVG converge into document_merge_data_layout (56) with the authored .indd and the roster CSV, resolving @image (per-SKU photo) and @Wordmark (shared mark) into the template's two image frames, one merged sheet per row; document_render_layout (57) exports the whole merged document once to the press-ready PDF (page-count = row-count = 8, flagship page 1). Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the grades are NOT one recipe repeated — each neutralisation and each metal pass is a distinct per-frame, per-finish decision converging on the shared white point and the studio-silver target.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 57 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grade/mask/vectorize/halftone, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single upload and the four auto-straightens. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralisations is a DIFFERENT reasoned correction to the frame's own in-frame grey card (cool-cast frames warmed, warm-cast frames cooled, a green-cast frame corrected on the tint axis, a split-cast frame compromised, an over-exposed frame pulled down, a flat/under frame lifted with highlight discipline) all forced to converge on one measurable white point and brightness — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top is an agent-AUTHORED, primitive-built house look: a masked image_adjust_hsl metal pass per frame (the only masked-recolor path) that must hold each piece TRUE to its actual finish across THREE finishes (brushed, high-polish, oxidized) — the oxidized pieces held genuinely dark, the brushed/polished read crisp and cool-neutral — no preset, no auto-tone, no whole-image overlay. The endpoint is a genuine two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record .indd (the per-SKU packshot via @image, the shared vectorized wordmark via @Wordmark, so the wordmark reaches the masthead as a merge bind rather than banned free-form placement), plus two prep-before-trace vector disciplines (necklace silhouette + wordmark) and a screen-print halftone. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no 3D, no from-scratch art, no upscaling (camera-scale ~4200 px sources so the 2400x3000 hero and 300 DPI sheet frames are downscale-only), no compositing; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; image_remove_background never claims a see-through enclosed loop; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _highlights / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast are all replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION the agent can trip, not a self-measurement): the capsule ships in three real finishes and every frame carries an in-frame 18% grey card, and there are two trippable, invisible-until-inspected decisions. (1) Cross-asset neutralisation: each frame must be neutralised to its own card so the whole set shares ONE white point and brightness, which requires per-frame corrections of OPPOSITE sign (warm-lamp frames cooled, cool-window frames warmed) and on different axes (a green fluorescent frame needs a tint correction, not a temperature one) — a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the batch leaves the cool frames blue and the green frame green and fails, and the agent must REPORT its per-frame temperature/tint/exposure so 'matched' is checkable. (2) The FINISH TRAP: three SKUs (AF-204/205/208) are genuinely oxidized/antiqued — deliberately dark by design, their grey cards honest and neutral — so the correct move is to neutralise to the card and HOLD the patina; a naive agent that applies the same brighten-and-cool-to-crisp masked treatment used on the brushed pieces (or 'brightens silver because silver should be bright') lifts the patina and turns an antiqued piece into tarnished-looking brushed silver, misrepresenting the product. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset consistency to a measurable card target across eight differently-lit frames on opposite-sign, different-axis corrections; (b) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — a necklace has ENCLOSED interior negative space image_remove_background cannot punch, so the hero is placed by remove_background({backgroundColor}) onto a solid sweep (the interior correctly reads the sweep) NOT select->invert->fill_area (which bricks the loop with a hard plate), and the metal look is masked image_adjust_hsl NOT whole-image color_overlay or flat fill; (c) prep-before-trace discipline on both the necklace cut-out and the skewed off-white wordmark scan before vectorize; (d) a two-image-column one-file-per-row .indd merge (text-only document_merge_data_vector and a convert_pdf_to_indd target both fail to bind). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (stated as decoupled claims so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance) and one shared white point/brightness, evaluated on the eight RETAINED card-bearing neutralised masters, with the oxidized SKUs measurably darker than the brushed/polished ones (finish preserved); (b) card-EXCLUSION checked separately on the eight card-removed packshots and the 4:5 hero; plus the agent's reported per-frame WB/exposure and per-finish metal parameters, the hero at exactly 2400x3000 from camera-scale pixels, the necklace line-art and wordmark as clean prepared-then-traced vectors, and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8, flagship page 1).
